From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Longview Labs — exec approval request (price anchoring + renewal language)

Marissa / Kimberly —

Forwarding Longview’s ask. Summary of Deal Desk analysis below: 
- Requested uplift cap (6%) is tighter than our typical 8–12% band for multi-year public offers, but not impossible if Longview commits to a usage ramp and escrow-style protection.
- Renewal-protector clause (right to renegotiate or exit if list price increases) is a material revenue/retention risk. We can consider a limited protector tied to predefined triggers (e.g., material product pricing changes >10% or introduction of new mandatory surcharges).

Options to put forward for Exec sign-off: 
1) Anchor + Escrow: 3-year anchor with a portion of committed spend held in an escrow-like credit that compensates the customer if an uplift > cap occurs; allows us to preserve flexibility while giving Longview financial protection.
2) Fixed-Uplift Contract: 3-year firm uplift cap at 6% but no unilateral exit — requires revenue reserve and Exec approval for threshold.
3) Conditional Renewal Protector: allow a 60-day renegotiation window only if Redwood implements a platform-wide mandatory price change >10% (not ad-hoc regional surcharges).

Attachments: longview-deal-summary.xlsx with modeled revenue and suggested guardrails. I recommend Exec sign-off on option 1 or 3 with clear trigger definitions.

Aditya
Senior Deal Desk Manager

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Longview Labs — exec approval request (price anchoring + renewal language)

Team —

Thanks for the clear framing. A few directional points before I approve anything: 
- We should avoid open-ended exit rights unless Longview provides substantial reciprocal protections (minimum committed spend that is non-cancellable) or we establish a financial remedy (escrow/credit).
- If we permit an uplift cap at 6% we must model downside and confirm the revenue impact to FY29 guidance; I’ll need the numbers from Finance (copy Laura).
- For the renewal protector, I prefer Option 3 with a strict definition of triggering events. "Price changes" must be scoped to list price changes applied to all customers or new mandatory platform surcharges — not region-specific promos or negotiated surcharges.

Marissa: please get Longview to accept a conditional protector definition and commit to the spend profile. Aditya: work with Laura on the finance impact model; I want the P&L delta by EOD tomorrow. If the model looks acceptable, I’m prepared to sign off on Option 1 (Anchor + Escrow) with documented triggers.

-Kim
VP, Revenue Operations

If Longview confirms both, we will route the exec packet today. Also attaching our redlines for quick review.
